content.content:
**Music & Content ID (quoted from the FAQ)**

- Definition: "Content ID is YouTube's automated copyright detection system."
- Registered tracks: "Some contributors or their distributors may choose to register their tracks with Content ID."
- Shield icon: "Tracks displaying a shield icon are registered with Content ID and may trigger claims"
- Claim vs. strike: "A Content ID claim is not a copyright strike."
- Claim impact: "It does not affect your channel standing."
- Strike impact: "Three strikes can lead to account termination."
- Dispute option: "I have permission or a license to use the content"
- License certificates: "License certificates are available for tracks registered with YouTube's Content ID."
- Other tracks: "For other tracks, users should keep the download link, file name, and the Pixabay Content License"
- Avoiding claims: "Avoid uploading music-only content" is listed as a way to reduce flagging.
- Play counts: "We update play numbers once a day, so it will take up to 24 hours for you to see changes."

**Other music rules (paraphrased)**

- Commercial video use is permitted when the music is part of a larger creative work.
- Background or intro/outro use in podcasts and audiobooks is allowed.
- Selling a track on its own, unchanged, is not permitted.
- Attribution is not required, though crediting the creator is welcome.
- Using AI tools on a track doesn't change the license rules.

- License summary: https://pixabay.com/service/license-summary/

Links: [{"title":"How to clear a YouTube Content ID claim with a Pixabay License Certificate","url":"https://pixabay.com/blog/posts/how-to-clear-a-youtube-content-id-claim-with-a-pix-190/"},{"title":"FAQ","url":"https://pixabay.com/service/faq/"},{"title":"How to tag your music and sound effects on Pixabay","url":"https://pixabay.com/blog/posts/how-to-tag-your-music-and-sound-effects-on-pixabay-189/"},{"title":"Intellectual Property Explained - Pixabay","url":"https://pixabay.com/blog/posts/intellectual-property-explained-441/"},{"title":"Content License - Pixabay","url":"https://pixabay.com/service/license-summary/"},{"title":"Download free media from SergePavkinMusic","url":"https://pixabay.com/users/sergepavkinmusic-6130722/"},{"title":"Download free media from SPmusic","url":"https://pixabay.com/users/spmusic-34490764/"},{"title":"Favorite Work","url":"https://pixabay.com/music/corporate-favorite-work-168461/"},{"title":"Terms of Service - Pixabay","url":"https://pixabay.com/service/terms/"},{"title":"Pixabay License - What is allowed and what is not?","url":"https://pixabay.com/blog/posts/pixabay-license-what-is-allowed-and-what-is-not-4/"}]

Pixabay's own materials describe a clear process for clearing YouTube Content ID claims on its music, though some pages are a few years old.

- **What the certificate is for:** Pixabay says a Pixabay License Certificate can be downloaded to help clear YouTube Content ID claims, and that the file can serve as proof of rights. (You can also now download a Pixabay License Certificate to help clear Youtube Content ID claims.)
- **Where to get it:** Per Pixabay's FAQ, License certificates are available for tracks registered with YouTube's Content ID. For other tracks, users should keep the download link, file name, and the Pixabay Content License summary as proof of permitted use. The certificate is offered from the search results page after download or under the "Download" dropdown on the Media Details page.
- **How to dispute:** Pixabay's guide says to pick the license option in YouTube's dispute form, tick the permission box, and paste the certificate text from the downloaded .txt file into the rationale field. (Select 'License: I have permission or a license to use the content claimed in my video' > Continue; ... Tick the box for 'I have permission to use the content from the copyright owner.)
- **Outcome:** The processing time is up to thirty (30) days once you submit a dispute. The outcome will either be approved, rejected or expired. Your YouTube channel won't receive a strike if your request gets rejected.
- **Content ID vs. strike:** Pixabay says a Content ID claim does not affect your channel standing. Monetization can still be affected, since ads may be served against your content and you won't be able to monetize the video.
- **Caveat from creators:** Some Pixabay music pages by individual artists say the certificate is for monetized channels disputing claims and is NOT for songs, apps, music libraries! NOT for distribution to Content ID, Meta Audio Library, Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon, etc.

Note: the Pixabay blog and FAQ pages are dated (roughly 1,300–1,800 days old by the metadata), so YouTube's current dispute form may differ from the screenshots and steps described there.

content.text:
# Music sources and track shortlist for a monetized Shorts channel (90 to 160 s)

All quotes were relayed by the fetch tool's page reader, so they are short excerpts; re-check exact wording before printing them in the guide. Uppbeat and Artlist official pages could not be opened at all (see the final list).

## PART A. Licensing, price, Content ID risk

### 1. YouTube Audio Library
URL opened: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/3376882?hl=en
- **Price:** free.
- **Standard license:** "If you want to find music that has a standard YouTube Audio Library license that doesn't require attribution".
- **Creative Commons tracks:** "If you're using a track with a Creative Commons license, you must credit the artist in your video's description."
- **Content ID:** "Copyright-safe music and sound effects downloaded from the Audio Library won't be claimed by a rights holder".
- **Monetization:** "If you're in the YouTube Partner Program, you can monetize videos with music and sound effects from the Audio Library."
- **NOT VERIFIED:** the wording "Creative Commons Attribution 4.0". The page only says "Creative Commons license" and links to creativecommons.org/licenses/.
- **Risk:** lowest of all sources.

### 2. Pixabay Music
URLs opened: https://pixabay.com/service/license-summary/, https://pixabay.com/service/terms/, https://pixabay.com/service/faq/, https://pixabay.com/blog/posts/how-to-clear-a-youtube-content-id-claim-with-a-pix-190/
- **Price:** free ("Use Content for free").
- **Attribution:** not required. "You do not need to credit Pixabay or the contributor of Content when you use it" (terms).
- **Grant:** "irrevocable, worldwide, perpetual (or as long as allowed by law), non-exclusive and royalty-free right", "for commercial or non-commercial purposes" (terms).
- **Prohibited uses:**
  - "You cannot sell or distribute Content (either in digital or physical form) on a Standalone basis."
  - "You cannot use Content in any immoral or illegal way, especially Content which features recognisable people."
  - "You cannot use Content in a misleading or deceptive way."
  - "You cannot use any of the Content as part of a trade-mark, design-mark, trade-name, business name or service mark."
  - Content with recognisable trademarks or logos cannot be used commercially in relation to goods and services.
- **Content ID (FAQ):**
  - "Some contributors or their distributors may choose to register their tracks with Content ID."
  - "Tracks displaying a shield icon are registered with Content ID and may trigger claims".
  - "License certificates are available for tracks registered with YouTube's Content ID."
  - "For other tracks, users should keep the download link, file name, and the Pixabay Content License".
- **Clearing a claim (blog):**
  - The certificate is "from under the 'Download' dropdown from the Media Details page (for logged in users)."
  - In the dispute, choose "License: I have permission or a license to use the content claimed in my video".
  - Then "copy and paste the Pixabay License Certificate from the .txt license file you downloaded from Pixabay."
  - "The processing time is up to thirty (30) days once you submit a dispute."
- **Risk:** high for Shorts over 1 minute. A registered track can claim, the Short is blocked while the claim is active, and the dispute can take up to 30 days. Use only tracks without the "Content ID Registered" label.

### 3. Uppbeat
NOT VERIFIED on official pages. https://uppbeat.io/pricing and https://uppbeat.io/help/uppbeat-premium returned HTTP 429 on every attempt; the fastly-f.uppbeat.io mirrors returned 404.

Unverified search-snippet information only (not opened):
- Free account has a 3-download allowance that tops up by 1 each month.
- Free users have access to roughly 25 to 30% of the catalog.
- Free users must paste an Uppbeat Credit in the video description to prevent claims.
- Premium whitelists up to 3 YouTube channels, after which credits are not needed.
- Paid prices: not obtained.

### 4. Epidemic Sound
URLs opened: https://www.epidemicsound.com/pricing/ (plan prices did not render), https://www.epidemicsound.com/blog/artlist-vs-epidemic-sound/ (Epidemic's own blog, dated "Apr 1, 2026")
- **Price (own blog, not the pricing page):** Creator "$9.99 per month billed yearly, or $17.99 billed monthly." Pro "$16.99 per month billed yearly, or $39.99 billed monthly."
- **Clearing:** pricing page says "Music cleared for your channel."
- **Cancelling:** "If you cancel, you have until your plan's end date to use Epidemic Sound."
- **NOT VERIFIED:** that videos published during the subscription stay cleared forever. The help article (epidemicsoundhelp.com/hc/en-us/articles/26254650213266) returned 403. The search snippet of that article said content published while subscribed "remains cleared to monetize permanently" and that new content after cancelling is monetized by Epidemic Sound.
- **Risk:** low while subscribed and the channel is linked.

### 5. Artlist
- **Price:** NOT VERIFIED on Artlist's site (https://artlist.io/pricing returned 403). The only figure is from a competitor's blog (the Epidemic URL above): "Music & SFX Social: $9.99 per month billed yearly, or $14.99 billed monthly"; "Music & SFX Pro: $24.92 per month, billed yearly."
- **License after expiry** (opened https://help-center.artlist.io/privacy-terms/artlist-license/):
  - Pro: "you can keep using your Projects in the same media and monetize them forever, even after your subscription has expired."
  - Pro: "When your subscription expires, those Projects can remain published in any media, but any new projects will not be covered."
  - Social: "When your subscription expires, those Projects can remain published in your Channel".
- **Clearlist:** "If you don't add your channel or YouTube Projects URL to the clearlist, you may receive claims from Artlist Ltd".
- An older undated Freshdesk page (https://artlist.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/43000669703-does-the-license-end-if-my-subscription-expires-) says "your license is valid forever, even if your subscription expires!". Treat the help-center license page as the current one.

### 6. Incompetech (Kevin MacLeod)
URLs opened: https://incompetech.com/music/royalty-free/faq.html, https://incompetech.com/music/royalty-free/licenses/, https://incompetech.com/music/royalty-free/youtube-contentid.html, https://incompetech.com/music/royalty-free/youtubeFAQ.html, https://incompetech.com/
- **License:** CC BY 4.0, stated site-wide in the FAQ. The licenses page says "Creative Commons — Free": "No charge. Requires that you credit the music."
- **Per-track 3.0 vs 4.0:** NOT VERIFIED. pieces.json has no license field and the per-track pages are JavaScript-rendered.
- **Attribution format (FAQ):**

Title Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com)
Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

- **Monetization:** "Yes. Please use my music to make money on YouTube."
- **No-attribution Standard License:** it exists, paid by PayPal, but its price is NOT VERIFIED (the licenses page showed no amount). An unverified Wikipedia mirror cites $30 for one track, $50 for two, $20 each for three or more.
- **Content ID:** yes, claims can happen.
  - Cause: "Probably has something to do with the Attribution part of the license."
  - Fix: put the credit in the description, then dispute. "The claim will come directly from YouTube, and be released within 72 hours and likely much faster."
  - Homepage, April 2, 2026: "We are still working to allow-list all my music by default, but that is not currently the case."
  - Homepage, May 7, 2026: "we are still progressing on getting my music cleared on Spotify Podcast platforms and on YouTube."
- **Risk:** medium. Always put the credit in the description at upload; a claim on a Short over 1 minute blocks it until released.

### 7. Free Music Archive
URLs opened: https://freemusicarchive.org/faq, https://freemusicarchive.org/License_Guide
- **Per-track licenses:** "On the left side of the track page, you will see the specific Creative Commons license attached to the track."
- **Monetized use:** if ad revenue is involved, "you can only use Creative Commons music that allows for commercial use."
- **Usable in a monetized video:** CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC0. "You can put this song in a video or other derivative work." and "You can use it for commercial purposes."
- **Not usable, NC:** "You cannot use it for commercial purposes."
- **Not usable, ND:** "Syncing a track to video/moving images constitutes a derivative work, which is prohibited by this licence." FMA is categorical on this, not doubtful.
- **Attribution:** "One condition of all CC licences is attribution."
- **Content ID:** FMA notes some artists use it. "When your video is flagged, reach out to the artists themselves."
- **Risk:** medium to high, and resolution depends on each artist.

### 8. YouTube rules for Shorts
URL opened: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877?hl=en (title "Understand three-minute YouTube Shorts")
- "Shorts longer than one minute that have an active Content ID claim, regardless of the policy, will be blocked on YouTube."
- "Any Short that is over one minute in duration with an active copyright claim of any type, including manual claims," will be blocked globally.
- "The video will not be playable or recommended on YouTube, and will not be eligible for monetization."
- "There are no penalties to your channel."
- "Once the claim is resolved, your Short will be viewable and eligible for monetization."

URL opened: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12504220?hl=en
- "YouTube will split the revenue associated with its views between the Creator Pool and music partners".
- With 1 track: "half of the revenue associated with its engaged views would be allocated to the Creator Pool". With 2 tracks the Creator Pool gets one third.
- "Monetizing creators will keep 45% of their allocated revenue, regardless if music was used or not."
- "Shorts over one minute in length that contain claimed content are blocked and not eligible for monetization."

## PART B. Track shortlist
